text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
- Parliament began the debate on amendments to the constitution.
- Sources close to Prime Minister GYula HOrn said he had initiated talks with politicians whose parties may be expected to become decisive political forces after next year's elections.
- Investigations has failed to find out which government agency is to be blamed for the disappearence of a consignement of 10 tonnes of banknote paper.
- Free Democrat cabinet members are said to have opposed an agreement planned between the Vatican and Hungary on the financing of the Catholic Church.
- The government is expected today to discuss bills on shared apartment blocks and health and a survey conducted at privatization agency APV Rt.
- Italy and Hungary will set up a fund designed to help eliminate the Hungarian trade deficit with Italy and to support small and medium-sized enterprises.
- President Arpad Goncz said no final balance has yet been drawn up of the benefits and drawbacks of EU accession, as the EU is also facing changes, while Hungary itself is undergoing transformation.
- Hungary has fulfilled the terms for NATO integration, a committee of the US Congress dealing with security in Europe established in Washington Wednesday.
- President Arpad Goncz is due to pay an official visit to Romania between May 25 and 27.
- Privatisation agency APV Rt expects to meet its 180 billion forints income target for thisn year.
- With five million contracts concluded last year, the Budapest Commodity Exchange ranks 22nd among the world's commodity exchanges, and first in Central Europe.
- A violent storm and hail killed two men in Sopron (NW Hungary) on Tuesday.
The Finance MInistry plans to decrease taxes by 0.4 percent in real terms next year.
- The Hungarian banking system is underdeveloped, with 30-40 banks managing the finances of 300 large companies, Zsigmond Jarai, head of ABN Amro (Magyar) Bank said.
